narrative:
The model estimates your chance of failing the final year at 14%, meaning it expects about an 86% chance you will pass. Even so, the model’s decision rule has flagged you for remedial courses as a precaution; this is an early warning rather than a near-certain failure.

The strongest warning sign was your very high weekday alcohol consumption. This was the top-ranked factor and the only one among the three most influential features pushing the prediction toward failing. It stands out because, among students who passed, 84.5% reported very low weekday drinking and none reported very high use. The second most important factor was your record of past class failures: you have none, and that pushed toward passing. The third was your intention to pursue higher education; wanting to continue studying also pushed toward passing.

So the concern is not that you have a history of failure or low ambition—you do not. The concern is that high weekday drinking is the main risk factor in your profile. To improve your position, consider reducing or stopping weekday alcohol use, protecting regular study time, and actively asking for academic support when needed. Keep your goal of higher education visible, and build on your clean record of no past failures.
